brand.name: Park Season Guide
brand.tagline: Independent, unofficial help with timing a Disney park trip: when to go, what is running, and what it costs.

sisterSite.name: Ride Ready Guide
sisterSite.note: Our evergreen sister site. It owns the facts that do not move with the season: height requirements, ride-by-ride detail, accessibility, permanent dining, and park maps. We link to it rather than restate it.

meta.defaultDescription: Which month to visit Walt Disney World or Disneyland, which seasonal events are running, what a party night costs, and what is closed. Every dated claim carries the month it was last checked and how confident we are. Independent and unofficial.

author.name: The Park Season Guide editorial team
author.shortBio: Independent theme-park writers who track party nights, festivals, price changes, and refurbishment walls, and who label the difference between what has been announced and what we are only expecting.

legal.accuracyNote: Seasonal facts decay, so we date them. Every dated claim here carries the month a person last verified it, whether the operator has actually announced it or we are only expecting it, and the month it must be rechecked. Once that review month passes, the page says so automatically rather than waiting for us to remember. Confirm anything trip-critical with the operator before you book.

tickets.label: Undercover Tourist
tickets.note: Authorized reseller for both resorts. Worth checking before you buy park tickets direct, though hard-ticket event nights are almost always operator-only.

packagesDisneyland.label: Get Away Today
packagesDisneyland.note: Disneyland Resort ticket and hotel packages with layaway, which matters most in the peak Halloween and holiday windows.

gear.label: Amazon
gear.note: Rain ponchos, cooling towels, and the other seasonal gear a Florida August or a January evening in Anaheim actually calls for.
